Then the wretched brothers, the lords of the fortress,
when they perceived their coming,
went out at night, about two hundred horsemen and five hundred foot soldiers,
and laid an ambush in a ravine near the fortress.
And they dismounted from their horses and began to pitch their tents.
The force of the Franks fell upon them,
and destroyed the greater part of them with the edge of the sword;
and only a very few of them escaped.
And in the summer of this year,
those Persians who were of the house of Jalal al-Din Turan and of the house of Baba brought accusations against Mas'ud Bar Qawti,
saying that he had entered the treasury of Jalal al-Din
and stolen a large quantity of gold and precious stones.
And that Mas'ud was seized,
and from the bitter tortures they inflicted on him, he gave a bond signed by his own hand for fifty myriad dirhams.
And his cousin, whose name was Su'aydat, was condemned in judgment,
and was killed with the sword.
And a certain miller of Mosul, the son of Samaniyah, who had become a supporter of {OCR?} Mas'ud,
died under torture.
And another Kurdish Hakhari emir, whose name was Abu Bakr,
who for years had been a rebel in the mountains of Assyria,
and whom this Mas'ud had pacified
and brought to the Ordo,
he too was killed,
and eight of his companions with him.
And the eldest son of Sheikh 'Adi,
who had fled to Syria,
when he returned and went to the Ordo,
and began to make excuses for his flight,
was condemned and put to death.
And Mas'ud was brought to Mosul along with Mongol executioners to pay the gold.
And when he had remained with them for some days,
he fled from them by night.
And in the year 1593
(1593 of the Greeks) in the autumn season,
the armies of the Mongols went down again to Syria,
fifty thousand,
with Möngke Temür at their head,
the beloved brother of the King of Kings.
And Leon, king of Cilicia, also gathered his forces,
and went with him to his aid.
And the army of Egypt and Syria also assembled,
at their head being Alfi, who had become Sultan,
and Sunqur al-Ashqar as well,
because they had been reconciled with one another.
And the Tatars and the Egyptians clashed with one another between Hama and Homs,
on Thursday {OCR?}, the thirtieth of First Tishri of that same year.
